teaching.causalExplanation: Start with a plumber's quote. Three hundred and forty dollars plus GST. Plus GST means the GST hasn't been added yet. GST is a ten per cent increase, and last time a ten per cent increase was one multiplication. Times one point one. Three hundred and forty times one point one is three hundred and seventy-four dollars. That's the price including GST, what you actually pay. If you only want the tax itself, take ten per cent of the price before GST. Three hundred and forty times nought point one is thirty-four dollars. And three forty plus thirty-four is three seventy-four. Now the other direction. A laptop costs one thousand six hundred and twenty-eight dollars, including GST. What was it before the GST went on? Going forwards, you multiplied by one point one. So going backwards, you divide by one point one. Sixteen twenty-eight divided by one point one is fourteen hundred and eighty dollars. Check it forwards. Fourteen eighty times one point one is sixteen twenty-eight. A tempting slip is to take ten per cent off sixteen twenty-eight, times nought point nine. That gives fourteen sixty-five twenty, and it's wrong. The ten per cent was ten per cent of fourteen eighty, not of sixteen twenty-eight. So how much of the sixteen twenty-eight was GST? Here's a picture that makes it quick. The price before GST is ten equal parts. The GST is ten per cent, so it's one more part, the same size. That makes eleven parts altogether. So the GST is one part in eleven of the price including GST. Sixteen twenty-eight divided by eleven is a hundred and forty-eight dollars. And fourteen eighty plus a hundred and forty-eight is sixteen twenty-eight. Notice that ten per cent of sixteen twenty-eight would be a hundred and sixty-two eighty, too much, because sixteen twenty-eight is eleven parts, not ten. Try a quick one. A fifty-five dollar haircut, including GST, is eleven parts of five dollars. So five dollars is GST, and fifty dollars is the price before GST.

Sixteen twenty-eight divided by eleven is a hundred and forty-eight dollars. And fourteen eighty plus a hundred and forty-eight is sixteen twenty-eight. Notice that ten per cent of sixteen twenty-eight would be a hundred and sixty-two eighty, too much, because sixteen twenty-eight is eleven parts, not ten. Try a quick one. A fifty-five dollar haircut, including GST, is eleven parts of five dollars. So five dollars is GST, and fifty dollars is the price before GST.

scenes.teachingReason: Back to the supermarket. Twenty dollars thirty altogether, but the bread, milk and bananas are GST-free. Only the chips and the soft drink carry GST. They add to eight dollars eighty. That's eleven parts, so the GST is eight eighty divided by eleven, eighty cents. So of the twenty dollars thirty, just eighty cents is tax. Dividing the whole twenty thirty by eleven gives a dollar eighty-five, which taxes the bread and milk as well. And notice that the GST was never added at the register. In Australia, shops show prices with the GST already in, so the price you see is the price you pay.

scenes.teachingReason: Overseas, it's the same kind of tax with a different name and rate. Many countries call it VAT, value-added tax. In the United Kingdom, VAT is twenty per cent. Say a hoodie in London costs thirty-six pounds, including VAT. The price before VAT is a hundred per cent, and VAT adds twenty, so a hundred and twenty altogether. That's five parts plus one part. So the VAT is one part in six. Thirty-six divided by six is six pounds of VAT, and the price before VAT is thirty pounds. New Zealand calls its tax GST, but it's fifteen per cent. A jacket at sixty-nine New Zealand dollars, including GST, was sixty-nine divided by one point one five, sixty dollars before tax, so the tax is nine. Each country sets its own rate, and rates can change, so count the parts for the rate you're given.
